passage: Sahil here, I live by the colony gate. Dolma, five, ran towards the road after her ball. Her mother called, "Dolma, stop!" and Dolma froze mid-step while the ball rolled on. A scooter passed. Her mother walked up and said, "Thank you for stopping." Dolma looked at the ball, then at her mother. I can't tell if she was scared or just startled. In all the weeks I've watched, her mother rarely raises her voice.

qa.q: What was Dolma chasing?
qa.a: A ball.

qa.q: What might Dolma have felt when she froze?
qa.a: Startled or scared, since she stopped instantly. She might also just have been surprised by the loud call.

qa.q: Why might it help that her mother rarely raises her voice?
qa.a: Warnings kept for real danger keep their power, so Dolma stops when she hears one.

qa.q: How might Dolma's mother feel after the scooter passed?
qa.a: Probably relieved and a bit shaky, hinted by her walking straight up to thank Dolma.

grounding: Shows a child hearing a caution and stopping to look, with an adult who keeps warnings for real danger, seen by a neighbour.

passage: On Monday Kashish said "careful" about a spoon, a crumb and a sock, and Sachin, four, kept running. On Wednesday he raced towards the balcony door and she said, "Sachin, stop." He kept going until she caught him. That night she decided to save her warning words for real danger. On Saturday, when he reached for the hot pan, she said quietly and firmly, "Sachin, stop. Hot." He froze, hand in the air, and looked at her.

qa.q: What did Kashish say when Sachin reached for the hot pan?
qa.a: "Sachin, stop. Hot."

qa.q: What does Sachin's frozen hand suggest he understood on Saturday?
qa.a: That this warning was serious, since her tone was quiet and firm and unlike her usual "careful". He could also just have been startled by her different voice.

qa.q: What did Kashish change, and why did it work?
qa.a: She stopped using warning words for small things and kept them for real danger, so they signal him to stop and look.

qa.q: How might Sachin have experienced all the "careful"s on Monday?
qa.a: As background chatter he had learned to tune out, so none of them stood out as urgent.

grounding: Shows a child who ignores constant cautions but stops for a rare, clear warning about real danger.

passage: Rain made the market road slippery, and Shalini had a heavy bag in one hand and Aditi's hand in the other. She didn't say “careful” at every puddle; Aditi splashed through them happily. Then a bike came racing round the corner. “WATCH OUT!” Shalini said sharply. Aditi froze and stepped back at once. The bike swerved past. Shalini knelt. “That's why I said it. Bikes can hurt.” Aditi nodded, eyes wide. “You said it loud.” “Only for real danger.”

qa.q: What came racing round the corner?
qa.a: A bike.

qa.q: What was Aditi feeling when she froze and stepped back?
qa.a: She was startled and a little frightened by the sharp warning, and she stopped at once to look.

qa.q: Why did Aditi react so quickly to “Watch out”?
qa.a: Because Shalini saved the warning for real danger and didn't say it at every puddle, so the words kept their power.

qa.q: How might Shalini have felt as the bike swerved past?
qa.a: She likely felt a rush of fear and then relief that Aditi stopped in time.

grounding: On a slippery market road, a child stops at once at “Watch out” because her mother keeps warnings for real danger.

passage: Minakshi Dadi said “Careful!” all day long: careful on the stairs, careful with the spoon, careful with the crayons. Shalini, five, had stopped even looking up. One afternoon in their flat, Shalini reached toward the iron, still hot on the board. “Careful!” said Dadi. Shalini kept reaching. Dadi grabbed her hand just in time. That evening Dadi said to Shalini's mother, “She didn't listen.” Her mother said gently, “Maybe too many carefuls. Let's save it for the hot iron and the road.”

qa.q: What was still hot on the board?
qa.a: The iron.

qa.q: Why might Shalini have kept reaching after Dadi said “Careful!”?
qa.a: She had heard it so often all day that she didn't treat it as a warning, so she didn't feel alarmed or stop to look.

qa.q: What did Shalini's mother suggest?
qa.a: She suggested saving “careful” for real dangers like the hot iron and the road, so the word keeps its power.

qa.q: How might Dadi have felt after grabbing Shalini's hand?
qa.a: She probably felt frightened and frustrated that Shalini didn't listen, before understanding why.

grounding: A grandmother's constant warnings lose their power, and a child fails to stop at a real danger until warnings are saved for real risks.

passage:
“Nazia, WATCH OUT!”
Nazia froze on the kerb. A scooter zoomed past.
Anand pulled her back and held her. “Are you okay?”
“Why did you shout, Abbu?” Her voice shook.
“Because the scooter was coming fast. I only shout ‘watch out’ when something can hurt you.”
“Only then?”
“Only then. When you hear it, you stop and look, like you just did.”
Nazia looked at the road. “I stopped fast.”
“You did. Now we hold hands and look both ways together.”

qa.q: What zoomed past the kerb?
qa.a: A scooter.

qa.q: What was Nazia feeling when she asked why Abbu shouted?
qa.a: She was frightened and shaky from the sudden shout and the scooter, and wanted to understand.

qa.q: What did Anand explain about “watch out”?
qa.a: He said he only uses it when something can hurt her, so she knows to stop and look when she hears it.

qa.q: How might Anand feel after pulling Nazia back?
qa.a: He is probably shaken and relieved, which is why he holds her and asks if she's okay.

grounding: A child stops at “watch out” on a kerb, and her father explains he keeps that warning for real danger.

passage:
Playground note from Reena, Wednesday

I try not to say "careful" all day. The children climb, jump and fall, and mostly I let them.

Today Kavitha was running towards the gate path, looking back at her friends, when a delivery cycle turned in fast. I called, "Kavitha, STOP! Watch out!"

She froze on the spot and looked round. The cycle swerved past her.

Afterwards she asked, "Why did you shout?" I said, "Because the cycle couldn't stop. I only shout like that when it's really dangerous." She nodded, and held the fence rail for a while.

qa.q: What turned in fast on the gate path?
qa.a: A delivery cycle.

qa.q: What was Kavitha probably feeling when she froze on the spot?
qa.a: She was most likely startled and frightened by the sudden shout and the cycle. Holding the fence rail afterwards suggests she felt shaken for a while.

qa.q: Why did the warning work so well?
qa.a: Because the warning is saved for real danger, the words still had power, so Kavitha stopped and looked at once.

qa.q: What would change if "watch out" were shouted all day for small things?
qa.a: Kavitha might start to ignore it, and at the real moment with the cycle she might not have stopped in time.

grounding: It shows a child hearing "watch out" as a signal to stop and look, and an adult keeping warnings for real danger so they keep their power.
